paper.title: An Omnibus Test for the Two-Sample Problem Using the Empirical Characteristic Function
paper.authors: T. W. Epps and Kenneth J. Singleton
paper.journal: Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation
paper.access_boundary: Publisher metadata and abstract plus the Stanford author bibliography were read. The article body was not accessible, so no complete-paper body read, hidden derivation, table value, or paper-file hash is claimed.

bounded_read.source_scope_read: complete scipy.stats.epps_singleton_2samp implementation and immediately associated documentation
verified_claims: the test compares whether two samples have the same underlying distribution
the empirical characteristic function uses default positive points 0.4 and 0.8
the points are divided by the pooled semi-interquartile range
the feature order is cosine at each point followed by sine at each point
the implementation uses biased within-sample covariance estimates
the pooled covariance is n/nx times cov_x plus n/ny times cov_y
the statistic is n times the quadratic form of the feature-mean difference
the reference distribution is chi-square with covariance-inverse rank degrees of freedom
the small-sample correction applies only when both sample maxima are below 25
continuous samples with at least 25 observations each are the documented recommended domain

claim_boundary: The records support the named empirical-characteristic-function two-sample method and exact pinned implementation arithmetic only. They do not test WTI, fixed 25-by-25 daily-return blocks, the chi-square-four median gate, cumulative-return continuation, CFDs, fixed risk, activity, or performance. The EA imports no SciPy, Python, executable source, optimizer, or trained output.
